episode: Boris Becker: Four Guilty Verdicts, Twenty Acquittals
assumptions: beat duration = narration words / 2.5 words per second
authentic share is an upper bound: a beat counts as real when it shows at least one authentic asset, even if graphics also appear

findings.name: AI-generated imagery
findings.standard: 0% (hard rule; none of the 28 non-AI-Tested reference videos shows any)
findings.why: Generated pictures read as artificial when used as decoration.

findings.name: Authentic media share
findings.measured: 27% of estimated time shows at least one authentic asset (upper bound)
findings.standard: reference band 35-99% real captured (sampled; -12 points tolerance); band wider than 60 points, advisory only
findings.why: The references that look least artificial are built on real captured material; constructed graphics should explain what real media cannot.
findings.evidence: VISUAL-EDITING-RESEARCH.md section 3 (5 videos, FRONTLINE PBS | Official, SunnyV2, Themaxready)

findings.name: All-constructed stretch
findings.standard: longest in the references 90 s (sampled runs of 15 s); FAIL above 1.5x
findings.why: Long runs of graphics without any real picture are the 'AI slideshow' pattern the references avoid.

findings.name: Caption / text overlay share
findings.measured: 0% of time on beats that carry an editorial caption or kicker (labels, badges and credits are not counted)
findings.why: Text on every scene is not what the references do; labels belong to key terms, footage and credits.

findings.name: Repeated media
findings.standard: no asset on more than 2 beats (author's rule; no reference measurement)
findings.why: Repeating one picture reads as generic filler.

findings.name: Credit on every third-party picture
findings.measured: every authentic picture has a credit field in its scene
findings.standard: 100% (hard rule; the references show credit or source lines on borrowed material)
findings.why: CLAUDE.md: no media without a recorded source; references credit borrowed clips on screen.

findings.name: Licence and source recorded
findings.standard: every asset has licence, source URL and commercial use allowed (hard rule)

findings.name: Media permissions verified
findings.measured: every used asset is cleared by its recorded licence
findings.standard: usable = yes for every used asset (page screenshots of third-party sites are 'owner decision': quotation/commentary, not a licence)
findings.why: A recorded source is not permission to use.

findings.name: Long unchanging visual
findings.measured: longest single beat 35 s (beat length, not measured change)
findings.standard: longest static stretch in the references 26 s (frame-difference score); flag above max(60 s, that)
findings.why: A beat that long needs internal change (camera move, reveal, new panel) or a cut to real media.

findings.name: Scene-change rate
findings.measured: 3.7 beats/min (a beat can contain several internal changes)
findings.why: Compare only as an indication: beats are not shots.

findings.name: Visual matches narration (lexical screen only)
findings.measured: 5 real pictures share no content word with their narration: C01:becker-2018.jpg, C01:gov-convicted-0.jpg, C01:gov-convicted-0.jpg, C02:becker-action-1994.jpg, C10:gov-convicted-0.jpg
findings.standard: a person confirms each flagged picture shows what is said (a word match is not proof of relevance)
findings.why: A picture unrelated to the narration is the strongest 'filler' signal.

findings.name: Every cue has an editorial purpose
findings.measured: 0 of 10 cues without a written purpose
findings.standard: every cue states its purpose (hard rule from the directive)
findings.why: Random effects are the failure to avoid.

findings.name: Effect density
findings.standard: provisional cap 4 per minute: author's judgement, the reference set gives no effect count

findings.name: Music/ambience competes with narration
findings.measured: 6 beds, all at least 20 dB below speech
findings.standard: bed at least 20 dB below speech (lowest reference value 19.7 dB)
findings.why: A bed louder than that competes with the voice.

findings.name: Assets approved for use
findings.measured: 5 asset(s) not yet approved by listening: AMB_ROOM_TONE (pending human audition), SFX_PAPER (pending human audition), SFX_RISER (pending human audition), SFX_IMPACT (needs correction before audition), SFX_GAVEL (needs correction before audition)
findings.standard: every asset in a render has a recorded listening approval
findings.why: No asset has been auditioned; this stays a WARN until a person approves them.

findings.name: Audio assets exist
findings.measured: all cue assets are in the library
findings.why: A missing file produces silence or an error at render.

findings.name: Music repeated across channels
findings.measured: no music bed in this cue sheet
findings.standard: one bed per channel (hard rule from the directive: do not reuse one track across every channel)
findings.why: Identical music across channels makes the network sound templated.

findings.name: Final loudness and true peak
findings.measured: no mix has been rendered for this channel (stills phase; only the AI Tested demo chain was exported and measured)
